summary: Three years after the 1906 fire the city was still paying for the cisterns it sank under this neighbourhood's crossings — Laguna and Union, Buchanan and California, Greenwich and Webster — so that the next fire would have water. In the same years it was licensing horses one by one behind Lombard and Chestnut Streets, granting Aldonse Dialot a hand-powered laundry on Filbert, and letting the Presidio and Ferries Railroad string an overhead trolley through the streets.
